title: PRISM Finding
description: One finding produced by one detector. Structured evidence, never prose. Every number the user sees is a formatted string in slots; every number a chart or a test reads is a raw value in evidence.aggregates. See docs/vision/03_ARCHITECTURE.md section 3.5.

id.description: Deterministic for a given detector, title, columns and slots, so a user's answers stay attached to the same card across runs of the same file.

confidence.description: An enum, not a float. A rule fired or did not; a statistical finding carries its p-value and effect size in aggregates; a heuristic says so.

title_key.description: A template key, never a sentence. The UI owns the words.

slots.description: Engine-formatted strings that fill the template. Formatting lives in Python where it is tested once.

row_indices.description: Zero-based positions in the file as loaded, capped; row_count carries the full number.

aggregates.description: Raw values: counts, rates, effect sizes, p-values, tables. NaN is forbidden on the wire; absent values are null.

hypotheses.description: Closed list of template keys for how the finding could be innocent or otherwise. Never free text.

follow_ups.description: Grounded queries the engine can answer with one click. Generated from the finding type and the schema, so always answerable.

reproduce.description: How to recompute the headline number without PRISM, in spreadsheet terms.

extra.description: Detector-specific structured detail that does not fit the shared fields. Must remain optional for every consumer.
